Summary: The sources indicate that context collapse in digital spaces refers to the flattening of audiences into a single context, destabilizing individual self-presentation and collapsing identities (Sarmiento et al., 2024). They also discuss the impact of large language models (LLMs) on public debate, noting that these systems can shift reader beliefs, narrow perspectives, and amplify dominant arguments (Wu et al., 2025; Zhang et al., 2025b; Shumailov et al., 2024). Additionally, the sources highlight the increasing tech-driven nature of the "new normal" in 2025, presenting both challenges and opportunities, such as the rise of cyber-sacking and the amplification of both positive and negative human behaviors (Pew Research, 2021).
